2: 3: 4: 5: # Vigil 6: 7: ### A self-hostable proactive AI assistant with approval-gated sandboxed execution 8: 9: Vigil watches your inbox, tasks, and deadlines. It triages each event with a cheap classifier, 10: sends you an action card, and runs the long jobs inside a Docker sandbox. 11: Every action that leaves your machine waits for your approval. 12: 13: [Quickstart](#quickstart) · [Architecture](#architecture) · [API](#api-surface) · [Documentation](#documentation) · [Contributing](#contributing) 14: 15: [![CI](https://github.com/awun8191/vigil/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/awun8191/vigil/actions/workflows/ci.yml) 16: ![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue) 17: ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.12%2B-3776AB?logo=python&logoColor=white) 18: ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-0.115%2B-009688?logo=fastapi&logoColor=white) 19: ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-16%20%2B%20pgvector-4169E1?logo=postgresql&logoColor=white) 20: ![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-612-informational) 21: ![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-alpha-orange) 22: 23:
24: 25: --- 26: 27: ## What Vigil is 28: 29: Vigil is an autonomous personal assistant that you run on your own server. 30: It polls your connected accounts, decides which events need attention, and turns them into cards. 31: A card carries a summary, a priority, and a set of actions. 32: You approve or reject each action on the web client. 33: 34: Approved work runs in a sandbox container. The sandbox has a fixed tool schema, a memory cap, a CPU cap, and a workspace quota. 35: Vigil never holds a shell open on the host. 36: 37: The runtime keeps no state in memory between turns. 38: A run that waits for you is a set of database rows, not a sleeping process. 39: An approval that arrives three days later resumes the run in a new container. 40: 41: Batteries included: one PostgreSQL instance runs the relational state, the job queue, and the vector memory. 42: You do not need Redis, Celery, or a separate vector database. 43: 44: ## Why Vigil exists 45: 46: | Problem in a typical agent framework | What Vigil does instead | 47: | --- | --- | 48: | Execution state lives in a Python thread or generator | Run state is a database row. A paused run frees its process. | 49: | Parallel tool calls break the provider protocol | A barrier synchronizer satisfies every tool call ID before the next model turn. | 50: | Redis, Celery, and a vector database for one assistant | One PostgreSQL 16 instance runs the queue, the state, and the memory. | 51: | Integrations hard-coded into the agent loop | MCP connectors with an approval policy for each tool. | 52: | The agent runs shell commands on your host | A fixed-schema runner executes inside a capped container. | 53: | A restart loses every queued run | The queue uses `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and a heartbeat reaper. | 54: 55: ## Architecture 56: 57: ```mermaid 58: flowchart LR 59: G[Gmail connector] --> T[Triage
Jev classifier] 60: M[Other MCP connectors] --> T 61: T --> Q[(PostgreSQL 16
jobs, runs, cards, memory)] 62: Q --> C[Action cards
web client] 63: C -->|approval| W[Worker
6-stage loop] 64: W --> B[Barrier
synchronizer] 65: B --> S[Sandbox
Docker runner] 66: B -->|external side effect| H[Human
approval] 67: H -->|decision| B 68: S --> Q 69: W --> Q 70: ``` 71: 72: The loop has six stages: load context, compact context, call the model, partition the tool calls, execute, and persist. 73: The partition step splits parallel tool calls into immediate work, background jobs, and gated approvals. 74: The barrier holds the turn open until every tool call ID has a result row. 75: 76: ## Features 77: 78: | Subsystem | What it does | 79: | --- | --- | 80: | **Stateless runtime** | Runs move through `QUEUED`, `RUNNING`, `AWAITING_APPROVAL`, `AWAITING_BACKGROUND_JOB`, `COMPLETED`, and `FAILED`. The process exits at each pause. | 81: | **Barrier synchronizer** | Groups parallel tool calls and persists partial results, so a resume keeps the provider protocol valid. | 82: | **Postgres job queue** | Claims work with `SKIP LOCKED` and ages the priority. A reaper recovers a job when the heartbeat stops for 90 seconds. | 83: | **Long-term memory** | `pgvector` with 384 dimension vectors, a time decay with a 30 day half-life, a 0.35 floor, and a 0.65 override threshold. | 84: | **Context compaction** | Counts tokens with the model tokenizer, then applies a two-tier summary. An artifact becomes a stub, not a truncation. | 85: | **Proactive triage** | Batches connector items into one cheap classifier call, then converts the result into cards with an action set. | 86: | **Sandbox runner** | Fixed tool schema, CPU and memory caps, a workspace quota, and a snapshot on every pause. | 87: | **MCP connectors** | Gmail ships in the box. Calendar, Slack, and GitHub follow the same connector protocol. | 88: | **Skills** | Install, list, toggle, and remove a skill pack from the API. | 89: | **Device pairing** | A QR code on boot, a short-lived pairing code, SHA-256 token hashes, and AES-256-GCM secret storage. | 90: | **Web client** | React 19 and Vite. Home briefing, streaming chat, and settings pages. A monochrome design system. | 91: 92: ## Quickstart 93: 94: ### Requirements 95: 96: - Docker with the Compose plugin 97: - Python 3.12 or newer and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for local development 98: - PostgreSQL 16 with the `pgvector` extension, only when you do not use Compose 99: 100: ### Run the stack 101: 102: ```bash 103: git clone https://github.com/awun8191/vigil.git 104: cd vigil 105: 106: export SECRET_KEY=REDACTED rand -hex 32) 107: docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up --build 108: ``` 109: 110: The API listens on `http://localhost:8000`. 111: Check readiness: 112: 113: ```bash 114: curl -fsS http://localhost:8000/api/v1/health/ready 115: ``` 116: 117: On boot the API prints a pairing QR code and a short code such as `VIG-7K2M4Q`. 118: Open the web client and pair the device with that code. 119: 120: ### Run the backend from source 121: 122: ```bash 123: cd backend 124: uv sync 125: cp .env.example .env # set DATABASE_URL and SECRET_KEY 126: uv run alembic upgrade head 127: uv run uvicorn src.main:app --reload --port 8000 128: ``` 129: 130: Start the worker in a second terminal: 131: 132: ```bash 133: cd backend 134: env -u PYTHONPATH uv run python -m src.worker 135: ``` 136: 137: The API does not poll the job queue. It has no Docker socket, so a job it 138: claimed would fail at its first sandbox tool call. For single-process local 139: development you can set `EMBED_WORKER=true` and skip the second terminal, but 140: then the API process must own the Docker socket. Keep it false whenever 141: `python -m src.worker` runs. 142: 143: ### Run the web client 144: 145: ```bash 146: cd web 147: npm install 148: npm run dev # fixture data, no backend 149: npm run dev:live # talks to the API on port 8000 150: ``` 151: 152: ### Run the tests 153: 154: ```bash 155: cd backend 156: env -u PYTHONPATH uv sync --quiet 157: env -u PYTHONPATH uv run pytest -q 158: ``` 159: 160: The suite has 612 tests. Tests that need PostgreSQL or Docker skip when the service is absent. 161: Read the skip count before you read the pass count. 162: 163: ## Configuration 164: 165: Vigil reads environment variables through `pydantic-settings`. 166: The full list is in [`backend/.env.example`](backend/.env.example). 167: These keys matter most: 168: 169: | Key | Default | Purpose | 170: | --- | --- | --- | 171: | `SECRET_KEY` | none, required | Encrypts stored connector credentials. Generate it with `openssl rand -hex 32`. | 172: | `DATABASE_URL` | `REDACTED` | Async PostgreSQL DSN. | 173: | `APP_ENV` | `development` | `development`, `staging`, `production`, or `test`. A production boot refuses the default key. | 174: | `PORT` | `8000` | API port. | 175: | `JEV_API_KEY` | empty | Key for the cheap triage classifier. | 176: | `FAST_LLM_MODEL` | `gpt-4o-mini` | Model for summaries and compaction. | 177: | `REASONING_LLM_MODEL` | `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` | Model for the tool loop. | 178: | `EMBEDDING_MODEL` | `bge-small-en-v1.5` | Local int8 ONNX embedder, 384 dimensions, CLS pooling. | 179: | `MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_HALF_LIFE_DAYS` | `30.0` | Decay rate for memory scores. | 180: | `SANDBOX_IMAGE` | `vigil-sandbox:latest` | Image for the sandbox runner. | 181: | `WORKSPACE_BASE_PATH` | `/var/vigil/workspaces` | Host path for workspace snapshots. | 182: 183: Money is stored as `cost_micros`, an integer count of micro-USD. No column holds a float. 184: 185: ## API surface 186: 187: The service exposes 46 paths under `/api/v1`. Every module follows the same contract: a `repository.py` of Protocols, a `service.py` with the mechanism, and a `build__router(settings)` factory. 188: 189: | Module | Example paths | 190: | --- | --- | 191: | `health` | `GET /health`, `GET /health/live`, `GET /health/ready` | 192: | `auth` | `POST /auth/pair`, `GET /auth/me`, `POST /auth/revoke` | 193: | `cards` | `GET /cards`, `POST /cards`, `PATCH /cards/{id}`, `POST /cards/{id}/feedback` | 194: | `triage` | `GET /triage/recent`, `POST /triage/items/{id}` | 195: | `runs` | `POST /runs`, `GET /runs/{id}/steps`, `GET /runs/{id}/events`, `POST /runs/{id}/cancel` | 196: | `approvals` | `GET /approvals`, `POST /approvals/{id}/decision` | 197: | `chat` | `GET /chat/sessions`, `GET /chat/sessions/{id}/stream` (SSE) | 198: | `artifacts` | `POST /artifacts`, `GET /artifacts/{id}/download` | 199: | `memory` | `POST /memory/search`, `DELETE /memory/chunks/{id}`, `PATCH /memory/chunks/{id}/exclude` | 200: | `compaction` | `POST /compaction/dry-run`, `POST /compaction/run/{id}` |

"""Chat service implementing direct interactive conversation sessions.

A chat session is a thread row, its turns are rows of the unified ``messages``
table. Agent replies do not stream through this module: the in-app chat sends
a message by creating a run (``POST /runs`` with the thread as ``session_id``)
and the RunLoop persists each reply into the same table, so ``get_history``
returns the full conversation across both paths.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from src.config.exceptions import NotFoundError
from src.modules.chat.data import ChatMessageResponse
from src.modules.chat.repository import (
    ChatMessageCreateDTO,
    ChatMessageDTO,
    ChatRepository,
    ChatSessionDTO,
)
from src.modules.chat.state import InMemoryChatRepository, SqlChatRepository


class ChatService:
    """Chat service satisfying ChatRepository via duck typing.

    The constructor picks the repository: the SQL implementation on a request
    database session, the in-memory one when the service is built without a
    session (tests, the CLI harness).
    """

    _repo: ChatRepository

    def __init__(
        self,
        session: AsyncSession | None,
        settings: object,
        repository: ChatRepository | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.session = session
        self.settings = settings
        if repository is not None:
            self._repo = repository
        elif session is not None:
            self._repo = SqlChatRepository(session)

args.Content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ==============================================================================
# Vigil Assistant - Development Startup Script
#
# Starts the Website (React + Vite) and the Agents API (FastAPI) together,
# along with the background job worker for full agent loop execution.
#
# Usage:
#   ./start.sh [OPTIONS]
# ==============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Colors and formatting
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ -t 1 ]] && [[ -z "${NO_COLOR:-}" ]]; then
    C_RESET="\033[0m"
    C_BOLD="\033[1m"
    C_DIM="\033[2m"
    C_GREEN="\033[32m"
    C_CYAN="\033[36m"
    C_YELLOW="\033[33m"
    C_RED="\033[31m"
    C_MAGENTA="\033[35m"
    C_BLUE="\033[34m"
else
    C_RESET=""
    C_BOLD=""
    C_DIM=""
    C_GREEN=""
    C_CYAN=""
    C_YELLOW=""
    C_RED=""
    C_MAGENTA=""
    C_BLUE=""
fi

log_vigil()   { echo -e "${C_BOLD}${C_BLUE}[vigil]${C_RESET} $*"; }
log_info()    { echo -e "${C_BOLD}${C_BLUE}[vigil]${C_RESET} ${C_CYAN}INFO${C_RESET}  $*"; }
log_success() { echo -e "${C_BOLD}${C_BLUE}[vigil]${C_RESET} ${C_GREEN}OK${C_RESET}    $*"; }
log_warn()    { echo -e "${C_BOLD}${C_BLUE}[vigil]${C_RESET} ${C_YELLOW}WARN${C_RESET}  $*"; }
log_error()   { echo -e "${C_BOLD}${C_BLUE}[vigil]${C_RESET} ${C_RED}ERROR${C_RESET} $*" >&2; }

# Stream prefixer for child processes
prefix_stream() {
    local tag="$1"
    local color="$2"
    awk -v tag="$tag" -v color="$color" -v reset="$C_RESET" '{ print color "[" tag "]" reset " " $0; fflush() }'
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Root resolution
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
if [[ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/backend/pyproject.toml" && -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/web/package.json" ]]; then
    PROJECT_ROOT="$SCRIPT_DIR"
elif [[ -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/../backend/pyproject.toml" && -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/../web/package.json" ]]; then
    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
else
    log_error "Cannot locate Vigil repository root from $SCRIPT_DIR"
    exit 1
fi

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration & Defaults
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ENABLE_API=true
ENABLE_WEB=true
ENABLE_WORKER=true
EMBED_WORKER=false
RUN_MIGRATIONS=true
MOCK_MODE=false
RAW_LOGS=false
API_HOST="127.0.0.1"
API_PORT="8000"
WEB_PORT="5173"

# Read defaults from .env if present
if [[ -f "$PROJECT_ROOT/backend/.env" ]]; then
    ENV_PORT=$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*PORT=' "$PROJECT_ROOT/backend/.env" | cut -d '=' -f2- | tr -d ' "\r\n' || true)
    ENV_HOST=$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*HOST=' "$PROJECT_ROOT/backend/.env" | cut -d '=' -f2- | tr -d ' "\r\n' || true)
    ENV_EMBED=$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*EMBED_WORKER=' "$PROJECT_ROOT/backend/.env" | cut -d '=' -f2- | tr -d ' "\r\n' || true)
    [[ -n "$ENV_PORT" ]] && API_PORT="$ENV_PORT"
    [[ -n "$ENV_HOST" ]] && API_HOST="$ENV_HOST"
    if [[ "$ENV_EMBED" == "true" ]]; then
        EMBED_WORKER=true
        ENABLE_WORKER=false
    fi
elif [[ -f "$PROJECT_ROOT/.env" ]]; then
    ENV_PORT=$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*PORT=' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.env" | cut -d '=' -f2- | tr -d ' "\r\n' || true)
    ENV_HOST=$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*HOST=' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.env" | cut -d '=' -f2- | tr -d ' "\r\n' || true)
    ENV_EMBED=$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*EMBED_WORKER=' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.env" | cut -d '=' -f2- | tr -d ' "\r\n' || true)
    [[ -n "$ENV_PORT" ]] && API_PORT="$ENV_PORT"
    [[ -n "$ENV_HOST" ]] && API_HOST="$ENV_HOST"
    if [[ "$ENV_EMBED" == "true" ]]; then
        EMBED_WORKER=true
        ENABLE_WORKER=false
    fi
fi

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Usage / Help
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
show_help() {
    cat << EOF
${C_BOLD}Vigil Assistant Startup Script${C_RESET}

Runs the React Web UI and the FastAPI Agents API together for local development,
including the background job worker so agent runs execute end-to-end.

${C_BOLD}USAGE:${C_RESET}
  ./start.sh [OPTIONS]

${C_BOLD}OPTIONS:${C_RESET}
  -h, --help            Show this help message and exit
  --no-worker           Run only Website and API (do not start the background worker)
  --worker              Explicitly enable separate background worker (default)
  --embed-worker        Run worker embedded inside the API process (EMBED_WORKER=true)
  --api-only            Start only the Agents API (plus worker, unless --no-worker)
  --web-only            Start only the Website frontend
  --mock                Run the Website in mock simulation mode (no backend needed)
  --no-migrate          Skip database migrations (alembic upgrade head)
  --raw-logs            Do not prefix logs with [api], [web], [worker] tags
  --api-port PORT       Port for the Agents API (default: ${API_PORT})
  --api-host HOST       Host address for the Agents API (default: ${API_HOST})
  --web-port PORT       Port for the Web frontend (default: ${WEB_PORT})

${C_BOLD}EXAMPLES:${C_RESET}
  ./start.sh                  # Start Website, Agents API, and Worker together
  ./start.sh --no-worker      # Start Website and Agents API only
  ./start.sh --api-port 8080  # Start with custom API port
  ./start.sh --web-only       # Start only the Vite frontend dev server
  ./start.sh --mock           # Run frontend with mock/fixture data

EOF
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parse CLI arguments
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        -h|--help)
            show_help
            exit 0
            ;;
        --no-worker)
            ENABLE_WORKER=false
            shift
            ;;
        --worker)
            ENABLE_WORKER=true
            EMBED_WORKER=false
            shift
            ;;
        --embed-worker)
            EMBED_WORKER=true
            ENABLE_WORKER=false
            shift
            ;;
        --api-only)
            ENABLE_WEB=false
            shift
            ;;
        --web-only)
            ENABLE_API=false
            ENABLE_WORKER=false
            shift
            ;;
        --mock)
            MOCK_MODE=true
            shift
            ;;
        --no-migrate)
            RUN_MIGRATIONS=false
            shift
            ;;
        --raw-logs)
            RAW_LOGS=true
            shift
            ;;
        --api-port)
            if [[ -z "${2:-}" ]]; then
                log_error "--api-port requires a port number argument"
                exit 1
            fi
            API_PORT="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        --api-host)
            if [[ -z "${2:-}" ]]; then
                log_error "--api-host requires a host argument"
                exit 1
            fi
            API_HOST="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        --web-port)
            if [[ -z "${2:-}" ]]; then
                log_error "--web-port requires a port number argument"
                exit 1
            fi
            WEB_PORT="$2"
            shift 2
            ;;
        *)
            log_error "Unknown option: $1"
            echo "Use ./start.sh --help to see available options."
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
done

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Process Management & Cleanup
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PIDS=()
CLEANING_UP=false

kill_recursive() {
    local parent="$1"
    local children
    children=$(pgrep -P "$parent" 2>/dev/null || true)
    for child in $children; do
        kill_recursive "$child"
    done
    if kill -0 "$parent" 2>/dev/null; then
        kill -TERM "$parent" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
}

cleanup() {
    # Guard against multiple executions
    if [[ "$CLEANING_UP" == true ]]; then
        return
    fi
    CLEANING_UP=true
    trap - SIGINT SIGTERM EXIT

    echo ""
    log_info "Shutting down Vigil services..."

    # Gracefully stop all recorded processes and their children
    for pid in "${PIDS[@]}"; do
        kill_recursive "$pid"
    done

    # Allow up to 2 seconds for graceful shutdown
    local waited=0
    while [[ $waited -lt 4 ]]; do
        local any_running=false
        for pid in "${PIDS[@]}"; do
            if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
                any_running=true
                break
            fi
        done
        if [[ "$any_running" == false ]]; then
            break
        fi
        sleep 0.5
        waited=$((waited + 1))
    done

    # Force kill any remaining processes
    for pid in "${PIDS[@]}"; do
        if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
            kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
    done

    log_success "All services stopped."
    exit 0
}

trap cleanup SIGINT SIGTERM EXIT

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pre-flight Checks
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
log_vigil "Initializing Vigil environment..."

# 1. Check uv package manager
if ! command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    log_error "'uv' is required but not found in PATH."
    log_error "Install uv via: curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh"
    exit 1
fi

# 2. Check Node & npm if web is enabled
if [[ "$ENABLE_WEB" == true ]]; then
    if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        log_error "'node' and 'npm' are required to run the web client."
        log_error "Please install Node.js v20+ from https://nodejs.org/"
        exit 1
    fi
fi

# 3. Check environment configuration
if [[ ! -f "$PROJECT_ROOT/backend/.env" ]]; then
    if [[ -f "$PROJECT_ROOT/.env" ]]; then
        log_info "Copying root .env to backend/.env..."
        cp "$PROJECT_ROOT/.env" "$PROJECT_ROOT/backend/.env"
    elif [[ -f "$PROJECT_ROOT/backend/.env.example" ]]; then
        log_info "Creating backend/.env from backend/.env.example..."
        cp "$PROJECT_ROOT/backend/.env.example" "$PROJECT_ROOT/backend/.env"
    fi
fi

if [[ ! -f "$PROJECT_ROOT/.env" && -f "$PROJECT_ROOT/backend/.env" ]]; then
    cp "$PROJECT_ROOT/backend/.env" "$PROJECT_ROOT/.env"
fi

# 4. Check backend python virtualenv
if [[ ! -d "$PROJECT_ROOT/backend/.venv" ]]; then
    log_info "Syncing Python virtualenv (uv sync)..."
    (cd "$PROJECT_ROOT/backend" && uv sync --quiet)
    log_success "Python virtualenv initialized."
fi

# 5. Check web dependencies
if [[ "$ENABLE_WEB" == true && ! -d "$PROJECT_ROOT/web/node_modules" ]]; then
    log_info "Installing web dependencies (npm install)..."
    (cd "$PROJECT_ROOT/web" && npm install --silent)
    log_success "Web dependencies installed."
fi

# 6. Database connectivity & migrations (if API or Worker is enabled)
if [[ "$ENABLE_API" == true || "$ENABLE_WORKER" == true ]]; then
    log_info "Checking PostgreSQL connection..."
    check_db_cmd="
import asyncio, sys
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import create_async_engine
from sqlalchemy import text
from src.config.settings import get_settings

async def check():
    settings = get_settings()
    engine = create_async_engine(settings.DATABASE_URL)
    try:
        async with engine.connect() as conn:
            await conn.execute(text('SELECT 1'))
        return True
    except Exception:
        return False
    finally:
        await engine.dispose()

if not asyncio.run(check()):
    sys.exit(1)
"
    if ! (cd "$PROJECT_ROOT/backend" && uv run python -c "$check_db_cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1); then
        log_warn "PostgreSQL is not responding on configured DATABASE_URL."

        # Check if docker container is present and stopped
        if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            pg_container=$(docker ps -a --filter "name=postgres" --format "{{.Names}}" | grep -E "v[i|r]gil-postgres" | head -n 1 || true)
            if [[ -n "$pg_container" ]]; then
                log_info "Found PostgreSQL Docker container '$pg_container'. Attempting to start it..."
                docker start "$pg_container" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
                sleep 2
            fi
        fi

        # Re-check connection
        if ! (cd "$PROJECT_ROOT/backend" && uv run python -c "$check_db_cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1); then
            log_error "Could not connect to PostgreSQL database."
            log_error "Ensure PostgreSQL (with pgvector) is running, or start it via Docker:"
            log_error "  docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up -d postgres"
            exit 1
        fi
    fi
    log_success "PostgreSQL is connected and healthy."

    # Run Alembic migrations
    if [[ "$RUN_MIGRATIONS" == true ]]; then
        log_info "Running database migrations (alembic upgrade head)..."
        (cd "$PROJECT_ROOT/backend" && uv run alembic upgrade head >/dev/null)
        log_success "Database schema is up to date."
    fi
fi

# 7. Check for port conflicts
check_port_in_use() {
    local port="$1"
    local name="$2"
    if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        if ss -tulpn 2>/dev/null | grep -E -q ":${port}[[:space:]]"; then
            log_error "Port ${port} (${name}) is already in use by another process."
            return 1
        fi
    elif command -v lsof >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        if lsof -i ":${port}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            log_error "Port ${port} (${name}) is already in use by another process."
            return 1
        fi
    fi
    return 0
}

if [[ "$ENABLE_API" == true ]]; then
    if ! check_port_in_use "$API_PORT" "Agents API"; then
        log_error "Please free port $API_PORT or run with --api-port <new-port>"
        exit 1
    fi
fi

if [[ "$ENABLE_WEB" == true ]]; then
    if ! check_port_in_use "$WEB_PORT" "Website"; then
        log_error "Please free port $WEB_PORT or run with --web-port <new-port>"
        exit 1
    fi
fi

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Start Services
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CHECK_HOST="$API_HOST"
if [[ "$CHECK_HOST" == "0.0.0.0" ]]; then
    CHECK_HOST="127.0.0.1"
fi

# 1. Start Agents API
if [[ "$ENABLE_API" == true ]]; then
    log_info "Starting Agents API on http://${API_HOST}:${API_PORT}..."
    if [[ "$RAW_LOGS" == true ]]; then
        (
            cd "$PROJECT_ROOT/backend"
            export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
            export EMBED_WORKER="$EMBED_WORKER"
            exec uv run uvicorn src.main:app --host "$API_HOST" --port "$API_PORT" --reload
        ) &
    else
        (
            cd "$PROJECT_ROOT/backend"
            export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
            export EMBED_WORKER="$EMBED_WORKER"
            exec uv run uvicorn src.main:app --host "$API_HOST" --port "$API_PORT" --reload
        ) > >(prefix_stream "api" "$C_CYAN") 2>&1 &
    fi
    API_PID=$!
    PIDS+=("$API_PID")

    # Wait for API readiness before launching frontend (up to 15 seconds)
    health_url="http://${CHECK_HOST}:${API_PORT}/api/v1/health/ready"
    log_info "Waiting for Agents API readiness at ${health_url}..."
    api_ready=false
    for _ in {1..30}; do
        if curl -fsS "$health_url" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            api_ready=true
            break
        fi
        if ! kill -0 "$API_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
            log_error "Agents API process exited unexpectedly during startup."
            cleanup
        fi
        sleep 0.5
    done

    if [[ "$api_ready" == true ]]; then
        log_success "Agents API is ready and serving requests."
    else
        log_warn "Agents API did not report ready within timeout (continuing anyway)..."
    fi
fi

# 2. Start Background Job Worker (if enabled and not embedded)
WORKER_PID=""
if [[ "$ENABLE_WORKER" == true && "$EMBED_WORKER" == false ]]; then
    log_info "Starting background Agent Job Worker..."
    if [[ "$RAW_LOGS" == true ]]; then
        (
            cd "$PROJECT_ROOT/backend"
            export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
            exec env -u PYTHONPATH uv run python -m src.worker
        ) &
    else
        (
            cd "$PROJECT_ROOT/backend"
            export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
            exec env -u PYTHONPATH uv run python -m src.worker
        ) > >(prefix_stream "worker" "$C_MAGENTA") 2>&1 &
    fi
    WORKER_PID=$!
    PIDS+=("$WORKER_PID")
    log_success "Background Agent Worker started (PID: ${WORKER_PID})."
fi

# 3. Start Website (Vite Dev Server)
if [[ "$ENABLE_WEB" == true ]]; then
    log_info "Starting Website (Vite Dev Server) on http://localhost:${WEB_PORT}..."
    web_script="dev"
    if [[ "$MOCK_MODE" == true ]]; then
        web_script="dev:mock"
        log_info "Running website in simulation mode (VITE_VIGIL_MOCK=1)."
    fi

    proxy_target="http://${CHECK_HOST}:${API_PORT}"
    if [[ "$RAW_LOGS" == true ]]; then
        (
            cd "$PROJECT_ROOT/web"
            export VITE_API_PROXY="$proxy_target"
            exec npm run "$web_script" -- --port "$WEB_PORT"
        ) &
    else
        (
            cd "$PROJECT_ROOT/web"
            export VITE_API_PROXY="$proxy_target"
            exec npm run "$web_script" -- --port "$WEB_PORT"
        ) > >(prefix_stream "web" "$C_GREEN") 2>&1 &
    fi
    WEB_PID=$!
    PIDS+=("$WEB_PID")
fi

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Banner Output
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
worker_status="Disabled"
if [[ "$EMBED_WORKER" == true ]]; then
    worker_status="Embedded in API process"
elif [[ "$ENABLE_WORKER" == true ]]; then
    worker_status="Active (PID: ${WORKER_PID})"
fi

echo ""
echo -e "${C_BOLD}================================================================================${C_RESET}"
echo -e "  ${C_BOLD}${C_BLUE}VIGIL AI ASSISTANT - SERVICES READY${C_RESET}"
echo -e "${C_BOLD}--------------------------------------------------------------------------------${C_RESET}"
if [[ "$ENABLE_WEB" == true ]]; then
echo -e "  ${C_GREEN}🌐 Website (Web UI):${C_RESET}     ${C_BOLD}http://localhost:${WEB_PORT}${C_RESET}"
fi
if [[ "$ENABLE_API" == true ]]; then
echo -e "  ${C_CYAN}⚡ Agents API:${C_RESET}           ${C_BOLD}http://${CHECK_HOST}:${API_PORT}${C_RESET}"
echo -e "  ${C_DIM}📚 API Documentation:${C_RESET}    http://${CHECK_HOST}:${API_PORT}/docs"
fi
echo -e "  ${C_MAGENTA}⚙️  Worker Status:${C_RESET}        ${worker_status}"
echo -e "${C_BOLD}--------------------------------------------------------------------------------${C_RESET}"
echo -e "  ${C_YELLOW}ℹ️  Pairing Note:${C_RESET} Enter the temporary pairing code printed above at"
echo -e "                 ${C_BOLD}http://localhost:${WEB_PORT}/pair${C_RESET} to connect your device."
echo -e "  ${C_DIM}🛑 Press Ctrl+C at any time to gracefully shut down all services.${C_RESET}"
echo -e "${C_BOLD}================================================================================${C_RESET}"
echo ""

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Process Supervision Loop
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
while true; do
    for pid in "${PIDS[@]}"; do
        if ! kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
            log_warn "A service (PID $pid) terminated unexpectedly."
            cleanup
        fi
    done
    sleep 1
done

120: ### Run the backend from source
121: 
122: ```bash
123: cd backend
124: uv sync
125: cp .env.example .env          # set DATABASE_URL and SECRET_KEY
126: uv run alembic upgrade head
127: uv run uvicorn src.main:app --reload --port 8000
128: ```
129: 
130: Start the worker in a second terminal:
131: 
132: ```bash
133: cd backend
134: env -u PYTHONPATH uv run python -m src.worker
135: ```
136: 
137: The API does not poll the job queue. It has no Docker socket, so a job it
138: claimed would fail at its first sandbox tool call. For single-process local
139: development you can set `EMBED_WORKER=true` and skip the second terminal, but
140: then the API process must own the Docker socket. Keep it false whenever
141: `python -m src.worker` runs.
142: 
143: ### Run the web client
144: 
145: ```bash
146: cd web
147: npm install
148: npm run dev          # fixture data, no backend
149: npm run dev:live     # talks to the API on port 8000
150: ```

156: env -u PYTHONPATH uv sync --quiet
157: env -u PYTHONPATH uv run pytest -q
158: ```
159:

### What the Startup Script Does

1. **Pre-flight & Environment Checks**:
   - Verifies prerequisites (`uv`, `node`, `npm`).
   - Ensures `backend/.env` exists (copies from template if needed).
   - Ensures Python virtual environment (`uv sync`) and Node dependencies (`npm install`) are ready.
   - Verifies PostgreSQL connectivity (and can start the container if Docker is used).
   - Runs database migrations automatically (`uv run alembic upgrade head`).
   - Checks for port conflicts on ports `8000` and `5173`.

2. **Synchronized Multi-Service Startup**:
   - **Agents API** (FastAPI / Uvicorn): Starts on `http://localhost:8000` (docs at `/docs`).
   - **Website** (React 19 / Vite): Starts on `http://localhost:5173` with proxying configured to the API.
   - **Agent Worker**: Starts the background job executor (`python -m src.worker`) so agent runs and chat actions execute end-to-end.

   - Clearly displays the terminal device pairing code and ASCII QR code emitted on API boot so you can pair at `http://localhost:5173/pair`.

4. **Graceful `Ctrl+C` Shutdown**:
   - Traps `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM` to recursively stop all child process trees (Uvicorn, Vite, Worker), preventing any orphaned processes or locked ports.

1: # Project: vigil-agent (Phase 1: Foundations & Architecture Scaffold)

3: ## Architecture
4: Vigil is an open-source, self-hostable proactive AI assistant and execution harness. Phase 1 establishes the rock-solid foundations and module-driven architecture scaffold:
5: - **FastAPI Backend (`backend/`)**: Modular architecture with dynamic router factories and ASGI middleware pipeline.
6: - **Strict Protocol Boundaries**: Every domain module defines persistence and external interaction solely through `@runtime_checkable typing.Protocol` abstractions in `repository.py`. Zero SQL, zero ORM, zero HTTP calls in `repository.py`.
7: - **Constructor Dependency Injection**: `service.py` implements all domain logic, accepting `session` and `settings` via constructor injection.
8: - **Factory Router Pattern**: Zero bare module-level global `APIRouter`s. Every module exposes `build_<module>_router(settings: Settings) -> APIRouter`.
9: - **Central Dependency Hub**: `backend/src/dependencies.py` re-exports all providers for one-stop injection.
10: - **Uniform Error Handling**: All errors inherit from `AppException` returning `{"code", "message", "request_id", "details"}` with correlation header `X-Request-ID`.
11: - **Security & Pairing**: SHA-256 token hashing, AES-256-GCM secret encryption, startup ASCII QR code pairing flow.
12: - **Containerized Deployment**: Multi-service Docker environment (`postgres` with pgvector, `api`, `worker`).

53: ## Interface Contracts
54: 
55: ### Error Response Contract
56: All error responses from FastAPI endpoints must conform to:
57: ```json
58: {
59:   "code": "ERROR_CODE_STRING",
60:   "message": "Human-readable explanation",
61:   "request_id": "uuid-string",
62:   "details": null | {}
63: }
64: ```
65: Headers:
66: - `X-Request-ID`: echoed from request or newly generated UUID.
67: - `X-Process-Time`: execution latency formatted e.g. `0.001234s`.
68: 
69: ### Router Factory Contract
70: Every module router must be defined as:
71: ```python
72: def build_<module>_router(settings: Settings) -> APIRouter:
73:     router = APIRouter(prefix="/<module>", tags=["<module>"])
74:     ...
75:     return router
76: ```
77: No module may define a bare global `router = APIRouter()`.
78: 
79: ### Repository Protocol Contract
80: Every `src/modules/<module>/repository.py` must contain:
81: ```python
82: from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable
83: 
84: @runtime_checkable
85: class <Module>Repository(Protocol):
86:     ...
87: ```
88: Zero imports of `sqlalchemy`, `sqlmodel`, `tortoise`, or raw SQL.
89: 
90: ### Security Contract
91: - `hash_token(token: str) -> str`: Returns SHA-256 hex digest.
92: - `verify_token(token: str, token_hash: str) -> bool`: Constant-time comparison.
93: - `encrypt_secret(plaintext: str, secret_key: str) -> str`: AES-256-GCM base64 encoded.
94: - `decrypt_secret(ciphertext: str, secret_key: str) -> str`: AES-256-GCM decrypt.
95: 
96: ### Auth & Health Wire Contracts
97: - `GET /api/v1/health` -> `200 OK` `{"status": "ok", "version": "0.1.0", "database": "connected" | "disabled"}`
98: - `POST /api/v1/auth/pair` with `{"pairing_code": "VIG-...", "device_name": "My Device"}` -> `200 OK` `{"device_token": "vgt_...", "device_id": "uuid", "device_name": "My Device"}`
99: - `GET /api/v1/auth/me` with `Authorization: Bearer vgt_...` -> `200 OK` `{"device_id": "uuid", "device_name": "My Device", "created_at": "...", "last_seen_at": "..."}`

29: ## 1. Executive Summary & System Philosophy
30: 
31: Vigil acts as an autonomous personal chief of staff. It continuously monitors incoming communication streams, tracked tasks, deadlines, and project milestones. Rather than passively waiting for user prompts, Vigil triages events using a cost-efficient decision model (Jev), surfaces actionable notification cards to a companion Flutter mobile app, and executes complex multi-step coding, document compilation, file transformation, and communication runs inside an isolated Linux sandbox under an approval-first security model.
32: 
33: ### Key Architectural Tenets
34: 
35: 1. **Approval-First Execution**: The agent can inspect files, write code, run compilers, and generate artifacts freely inside its isolated Docker sandbox. However, **any external side-effect** (sending an email, creating external drafts, publishing webhooks, modifying third-party accounts) strictly pauses execution and requires user approval via the mobile card UI.
36: 2. **Stateless Process Deallocation**: When an execution pauses for human approval or an asynchronous background task, the worker process **releases all memory and terminates**. Run state is serialized entirely within PostgreSQL. Approvals hours or days later resume execution seamlessly, surviving server restarts and container evictions.
37: 3. **Single Datastore Simplicity**: By running relational state, the atomic worker queue (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`), and vector memory (`pgvector`) within PostgreSQL 16+, Vigil eliminates the operational complexity of Redis, Celery, or external vector databases for self-hosters.
38: 4. **Decoupled Connectors via Model Context Protocol (MCP)**: External services (Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, GitHub) are not hardcoded into core application logic. They are implemented as standalone MCP connectors that expose polling capabilities and tools governed by standard approval policies.
39:

42: ## 2. Viability & Why Traditional Agent Architectures Fail
43: 
44: ### The In-Memory Trap
45: Most popular agent frameworks (LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, naive Pydantic AI loops) maintain execution state in the runtime memory of an async Python thread or generator:
46: 
47: ```python

49: async def run_loop():
50:     while not done:
51:         response = await model.call(history, tools)
52:         for tool_call in response.tool_calls:
53:             if tool_call.requires_approval:
54:                 user_ok = await wait_for_user_approval(tool_call) # BLOCKS IN-MEMORY!
55: ```
56: 
57: This pattern fails in production environments for four critical reasons:
58: 1. **Thread/Memory Exhaustion**: If a user takes 6 hours to respond to an approval notification, a worker thread or process remains locked in memory. At scale or on self-hosted VPS nodes, system resources are quickly exhausted.
59: 2. **Server Restart & Eviction Vulnerability**: If the server restarts, containers roll out, or a cold start occurs, all active, paused, or queued runs are dropped and lost.

1: # Contributing to Vigil
2: 
3: Thanks for your interest. This document describes how to set up the project, the rules that a change must follow, and the review gate.
4: 
5: Vigil is alpha software. The interfaces move. Open an issue before you write a large change, so we agree on the shape first.
6: 
7: ## Setup
8: 
9: Requirements: Docker, Python 3.12 or newer, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), and Node 20 or newer for the web client.
10: 
11: ```bash
12: git clone https://github.com/awun8191/vigil.git
13: cd vigil/backend
14: 
15: env -u PYTHONPATH uv sync
16: cp .env.example .env
17: ```
18: 
19: Start PostgreSQL with the Compose stack:
20: 
21: ```bash
22: docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up -d postgres
23: ```
24: 
25: Apply the migrations and run the API:
26: 
27: ```bash
28: uv run alembic upgrade head
29: uv run uvicorn src.main:app --reload
30: ```
31: 
32: The API does not poll the job queue by default, so a run you start stays queued
33: with no error. Run the worker in a second terminal:
34: 
35: ```bash
36: env -u PYTHONPATH uv run python -m src.worker
37: ```
38: 
39: For a single-process local setup, set `EMBED_WORKER=true` in `.env` and skip the
40: second terminal. Never do both: two pollers on one queue claim the same work.
41: 
42: The `env -u PYTHONPATH` prefix matters on a host that exports a Hermes or system `PYTHONPATH`. Without it, the interpreter loads a foreign `pydantic_core` and the tests fail at import.
43: 
44: ## Rules for a change
45: 
46: 1. **Module contract.** Every domain module under `backend/src/modules/` has five files: `repository.py`, `service.py`, `data.py`, `dependencies.py`, and `router.py`.
47:    - `repository.py` holds `@runtime_checkable` Protocols and DTOs only. No SQL, no ORM, no HTTP.
48:    - `service.py` holds the mechanism. It receives `session` and `settings` through the constructor.
49:    - `router.py` exposes `build_<resource>_router(settings) -> APIRouter`. Never a module-level `APIRouter`.
50: 2. **Models.** Every SQLAlchemy model declares `__tablename__` explicitly. Do not derive the name.
51: 3. **Money.** Store money in `cost_micros`, a `bigint` of micro-USD. Never use a float.
52: 4. **Embeddings.** Vectors are `Vector(384)` for `bge-small-en-v1.5`. Change the model in one place, not in a query.
53: 5. **Errors.** Raise a subclass of `AppException`. The response envelope is `{code, message, request_id, details}`.
54: 6. **Migrations.** Add a new revision under `backend/alembic/versions/`. Do not edit an applied revision. Check the highest number before you pick one.
55: 7. **Secrets.** Never commit `.env`. Never log a token, a key, or a decrypted credential.
56: 
57: ## Tests
58: 
59: Run the suite from `backend/`:
60: 
61: ```bash
62: env -u PYTHONPATH uv run pytest -q

import asyncio
from uuid import UUID
from sqlalchemy import text, select, func, case, or_, and_
from src.config.settings import get_settings
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import create_async_engine
from src.schemas.runtime import MessageModel

CHAT_HISTORY_ROLES = ('user', 'assistant')
session_id = UUID('a007cbba-203a-4811-8c69-ad424733c105')

async def main():
    engine = create_async_engine(get_settings().DATABASE_URL)
    async with engine.connect() as conn:
        no_tool_calls = case(
            (func.jsonb_typeof(MessageModel.tool_calls) == 'array', func.jsonb_array_length(MessageModel.tool_calls)),
            else_=0
        ) == 0

        has_content = and_(
            MessageModel.content.is_not(None),
            MessageModel.content != '',
        )

        filter_terms = (
            MessageModel.session_id == session_id,
            MessageModel.role.in_(CHAT_HISTORY_ROLES),
            or_(
                MessageModel.role == 'user',
                and_(MessageModel.role == 'assistant', no_tool_calls, has_content),
            ),
        )

        stmt = select(func.count(MessageModel.id)).where(*filter_terms)
        res = await conn.execute(stmt)
        print('Message count for session:', res.scalar_one())
    await engine.dispose()

asyncio.run(main())
"

# Vigil Backend Service

FastAPI backend engine, stateless agent runtime loop, and asynchronous task execution harness for Vigil.

Provides modular domain endpoints, pgvector long-term memory, PostgreSQL-backed `SKIP LOCKED` job queue, sandboxed Docker execution, secure device pairing, and strict protocol-driven repositories.

---

## Quickstart

### Prerequisites
- Python 3.12+ (CPython 3.12 or 3.13)
- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager
- PostgreSQL 16+ with `pgvector` extension (e.g. `docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up -d postgres`)

### Setup & Run

1. **Install dependencies**:
   ```bash
   uv sync
   ```

2. **Configure environment**:
   ```bash
   cp .env.example .env
   # Ensure DATABASE_URL and SECRET_KEY are configured
   ```

3. **Apply database schema migrations**:
   ```bash
   uv run alembic upgrade head
   ```

4. **Start the API server**:
   ```bash
   uv run uvicorn src.main:app --reload --port 8000
   ```

5. **Start the background job worker** (in a second terminal):
   ```bash
   env -u PYTHONPATH uv run python -m src.worker
   ```
   > **Note**: The API process does not poll the job queue by default. For single-process development, set `EMBED_WORKER=true` in `.env` to run the worker inside the API lifespan, or run the root startup script (`../start.sh`).

---

## All-In-One Startup Script

From the repository root, you can start the API, the worker, and the web frontend together:

```bash
../start.sh
```

---

## Architectural Invariants

Every domain module under `src/modules/` adheres to strict architectural contracts:

1. **Protocol Repositories (`repository.py`)**:
   - Defines persistence and external interactions strictly through `@runtime_checkable typing.Protocol` abstractions.
   - Zero SQL, zero ORM, and zero external HTTP calls in `repository.py`.
2. **Constructor Dependency Injection (`service.py`)**:
   - Accepts dependencies (`session`, `settings`, etc.) via constructor injection.
3. **Router Factory (`router.py`)**:
   - Every module exposes `build_<resource>_router(settings: Settings) -> APIRouter`.
   - Never defines a bare global module-level `APIRouter`.
4. **Uniform Error Serialization**:
   - All errors inherit from `AppException` and return `{ "code", "message", "request_id", "details" }`.
   - Propagates `X-Request-ID` and `X-Process-Time` response headers.
5. **Money**:
   - Stored as `cost_micros` (integer count of micro-USD). Never float.

---

## Testing

Run the test suite:

```bash
env -u PYTHONPATH uv run pytest -q
```

To run a specific test suite:
```bash
uv run pytest tests/unit/test_chat_sql_paging.py -v
```

I have resolved both errors and completed the documentation updates:

---

### 1. Fix: `cannot get array length of a scalar` in Chat History
* **Root Cause**: In [`SqlChatRepository._history_filter`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/chat/state.py#L200-L215), the SQL query executed `func.jsonb_array_length(MessageModel.tool_calls) == 0`. When a message's `tool_calls` column contained `'null'::jsonb` (JSON scalar null, as opposed to SQL `NULL`), `messages.tool_calls IS NULL` evaluated to `false`, causing PostgreSQL to attempt `jsonb_array_length` on a non-array scalar and crash.
* **Fix**: Wrapped the check in a SQL `case` expression:
  ```python
  no_tool_calls = (
      case(
          (
              func.jsonb_typeof(MessageModel.tool_calls) == "array",
              func.jsonb_array_length(MessageModel.tool_calls),
          ),
          else_=0,
      )
      == 0
  )
  ```
  This safely inspects `jsonb_typeof` first and short-circuits on non-arrays (SQL NULL, JSON null, and scalars) without errors.
* **Verification**: Added regression test [`test_history_handles_scalar_jsonb_tool_calls`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/tests/unit/test_chat_sql_paging.py) and verified session `a007cbba-203a-4811-8c69-ad424733c105` now loads smoothly.

---

### 2. Fix: `ValidationError: Input should be ... [input_value='message_delta']`
* **Root Cause**: In [`RunStepResponse`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/data.py#L50-L65), the `event_type` Pydantic `Literal` schema was missing `"message_delta"` (streamed message tokens) and `"compaction"` even though the agent loop emits `message_delta` steps.
* **Fix**: Added `"message_delta"` and `"compaction"` to `RunStepResponse.event_type` in [`backend/src/modules/runs/data.py`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/backend/src/modules/runs/data.py#L57-L66) and synchronized [`RunStepType`](file:///home/nasbombz/Documents/Projects/vigil-agent/web/src/types/index.ts#L170-L178) in the web frontend.

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm

# Install common utilities for agent execution and testing
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    curl \
    git \
    tar \
    gzip \
    unzip \
    procps \
    ca-certificates \
    build-essential \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install Node.js 22 LTS and npm from official Node image
COPY --from=node:22-bookworm-slim /usr/local/bin /usr/local/bin
COPY --from=node:22-bookworm-slim /usr/local/lib/node_modules /usr/local/lib/node_modules

# Ensure user 1000 exists (SANDBOX_USER in Vigil is 1000:1000)
RUN if ! id -u 1000 >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
        useradd -m -u 1000 -s /bin/bash vigil; \
    fi

# Configure npm global directory and cache writable by user 1000
ENV NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX=/workspace/.npm-global \
    PATH=/workspace/.npm-global/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH \
    NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules

# Create workspace directory with proper permissions
RUN mkdir -p /workspace && chown -R 1000:1000 /workspace

USER 1000:1000
WORKDIR /workspace

CMD ["/bin/bash"]
